statement: Let mu be a probability law with compact support of diameter at most D>0 and let R>0. Every local minimum of F(u)=integral ((x-u)^2+R^2)^(-1)dmu(x) has F(u)>1/D^2.
proof_text: At a stationary point set y=R^2, Z=integral ((x-u)^2+y)^(-2)dmu, and reweight dQ=Z^(-1)((x-u)^2+y)^(-2)dmu. Under Q, X=x-u is centered; let a=E X^2,b=E X^4. Normalization gives 1/F=(b+2ay+y^2)/(a+y). Differentiation gives F-second/(2Z)=3-4y E_Q[1/(X^2+y)]. If F-second>=0, Jensen gives y<=3a. The moment bounds then imply 1/F-D^2<=((y-3a)(y+a)+(4a-D^2)y)/(a+y)<=0. Equality requires y=3a,4a=D^2 and the symmetric endpoint law. For that law F(u)-F(0)=-u^4/[4a(16a^2+4au^2+u^4)]<0 away from zero, so equality is a strict maximum and cannot be a local minimum.

The same splitting at both 0 and a deterministic L proves the three-piece version Y(s)=B-mid(s) on [0,L] and Y(s)=B-mid(L)+B-plus(s-L) above L. Continuity and the Gaussian increment laws identify the two-sided Brownian law.

statement: Let K be a deterministic nonempty compact set and F a random closed set in Euclidean space. Suppose for 0<delta<=delta_0 that K has a delta-net with at most C delta^(-d_0) centers in K, and sup_(x in K) P(dist(x,F)<=2delta)<=C-prime delta^alpha with alpha>d_0. For R=dist(K,F), gamma=alpha-d_0 and A=C*C-prime, P(R<=delta)<=A delta^gamma and R>0 almost surely. For 0<p<gamma, E[R^(-p)]<=delta_0^(-p)+A*p*delta_0^(gamma-p)/(gamma-p), taking infinity^(-p)=0.
proof_text: If R<=delta, a closest point of K is within delta of F. A delta-net center is within 2delta of F, so a union bound proves the tail inequality. Letting delta decrease to zero excludes R=0. Compactness of K and closedness of F make disjointness equivalent to positive separation. Apply the layer-cake identity p integral_0^infinity delta^(-p-1)P(R<delta) ddelta, using the tail bound below delta_0 and probability at most one above it. Both integrals give the stated bound. The comparison tail delta^gamma on (0,1) has divergent gamma-th inverse moment, so the endpoint is not guaranteed.

statement: Every Cayley graph of a finitely generated residually finite group with a finite symmetric generating set is a local weak limit of finite quotient Cayley graphs, with generator labels preserved. For a prescribed radius R, choose a finite-index normal subgroup containing no nonidentity word of length at most 2R+1; every quotient root then has the exact radius-R labelled ball.
proof_text: Residual finiteness separates each of the finitely many nonidentity elements in the word ball of radius 2R+1 in a finite quotient. Intersect these kernels. A collision between two radius-R words would give a kernel word of length <=2R, and an extra edge between them would give one of length <=2R+1; both are excluded. Quotient transitivity makes every root exact. Letting R grow proves uniform-rooted local weak convergence. The labels are inherited from the quotient, so this is the labelled sofic special case.

statement: Let f:[0,1]->K be a homeomorphism onto a Jordan arc. Suppose for every n and 0<=j<4^n the subarc f([j/4^n,(j+1)/4^n]) is a similarity copy of K, and dim_H K=q. Then every nontrivial Jordan arc A contained in K has Hausdorff dimension q.
proof_text: The compact connected nontrivial set f^(-1)(A) is a nondegenerate closed interval [a,b]. Some base-four subdivision interval is contained in [a,b]. Its image is a similarity copy of K and hence has dimension q. It lies in A, while A lies in K; monotonicity of Hausdorff dimension gives q<=dim_H A<=q.

statement: A continuous planar path and its one-dimensional polygonal approximations do not by themselves produce a one-dimensional Jordan arc contained in the path image. For the standard Koch arc, the similarity dimension is log(4)/log(3)>1 and every nontrivial internal Jordan arc has that dimension. This deterministic obstruction refutes the generic polygonal-approximation route; it asserts no dimension above one for a Brownian trace.
